sentences.text: Pedeticosaurus was an extinct crocodylomorph, a member of the parent group Crocodylomorpha, that lived in South Africa during the Early Jurassic period.
The holotype specimen, which is the specimen the species is based on, is housed in the National Museum in Bloemfontein with the catalog number NMQR606.
In 1988, researchers C. E. Gow and James Kitching referred a second skeleton found in the Elliot Formation to the genus Pedeticosaurus.
The original describer, Van Hoepen, established a new family called Pedeticosauridae for the genus, believing it was closely related to Ornithosuchidae.
Later interpretations classified Pedeticosaurus as either a member of Sphenosuchia or Protosuchia, groups of small-bodied Jurassic crocodylomorphs.
In 1968, A. D. Walker erected the group Pedeticosauria, named after the genus, which is now considered equivalent to Sphenosuchia.
Gow and Kitching classified the second skeleton as Pedeticosaurus sp. and considered it a sphenosuchian.
In 2002, Clark and Sues reassigned the second skeleton to a new genus and species named Litargosuchus leptorhynchus.
The time range for this animal is estimated from 199.5 to 192.9 million years ago.
In 1986, James M. Clark proposed that Pedeticosaurus leviseuri was a synonym of Protosuchus haughtoni based on shared features like a broad scapula and large squamosal bone.
In 2002, Clark and Sues proposed that Pedeticosaurus leviseuri is a nomen dubium because the features of the holotype are too poorly preserved to distinguish it as a valid species.
